method: Historical findings were independently re-run against current HEAD and treated as hypotheses, not current authority.

findings.title: SVG serialization boundary
findings.reproduction: Pass an inert quote-terminated color followed by <g data-proof="inert"> through exportFigureSvg, exportFigureArtifacts, sceneToSvg, and resolvedSceneToSvg.
findings.observedBefore: All four paths serialized one extra proof element.
findings.observedAfter: All malformed colors are rejected as non-canonical #RRGGBB values; text is sanitized and XML-escaped; parsed structure remains fixed.
findings.regression: audit/current-head-hardening/test_svg_serialization.py parses XML produced by web/test/svg-serialization-cases.mjs and covers all four public paths.

findings.title: Functional tests and PR CI
findings.reproduction: Inventory committed audit commands and workflow triggers; run python3 -m unittest discover -v and npm test in web/.
findings.observed: Substantial regression machinery exists, but no workflow has a pull_request trigger; unittest discovers zero tests and npm has no test script.
findings.regression: No repository-defined required PR correctness check.
findings.futureWork: Required correctness floor / PR CI using today's explicit audits, nonzero case-count assertions, and check-only browser output.

findings.title: npm release workflow preflight
findings.severity: Release blocker for the next npm version
findings.reproduction: Resolve VERSION from web/package.json and check the workflow's expected release/npm/$VERSION manifest, tarball, and release/npm/README.md paths.
findings.observed: The workflow is manually dispatchable, but release/npm/ is absent, including release/npm/0.9.0-alpha.1/SHA256SUMS.txt and dist/figurestead-web-0.9.0-alpha.1.tgz.
findings.regression: No non-publishing preflight test exists.
findings.futureWork: Make dispatch unavailable until a candidate exists or restore a documented digest-bound candidate acceptance path.

findings.title: Portable-contract parity
findings.severity: P1 correctness and cross-runtime contract risk
findings.reproduction: Construct contracts with numeric title/series key, fps=0, negative marker size, scale padding 9, non-array annotations, and non-canonical colors in both runtimes.
findings.observed: Colors are now strict and path-aware. Python retains numeric title/key and fails fps=0 with ZeroDivisionError; browser rejects numeric title/key but accepts fps=0, negative marker size, padding 9, and coerces non-array annotations.
findings.regression: Only the SVG color boundary has a committed regression.
findings.futureWork: A bounded cross-runtime validation-policy package documenting strict/coercive behavior and adding path-aware parity fixtures.

findings.title: Semantic IDs and duplicate panels
findings.reproduction: Render series keys 'a b' and 'a-b', then inspect full mark IDs; separately create duplicate panel IDs in both contract paths.
findings.observed: The browser produces duplicate line/point and line/segment IDs for the collision pair; Python uses the same lossy stems. Both runtimes accept duplicate panel IDs.
findings.regression: No collision/uniqueness regression test exists.
findings.futureWork: A separately reviewed compatibility decision for stable escaping and duplicate-ID rejection, followed by migration tests.

findings.title: Core Python plotting input behavior
findings.reproduction: Call histogram with flat [1,2,3]; use two datasets/series with one label; pass incomplete and duplicate strip order; exercise non-finite inputs while counting open figures.
findings.observed: Flat histogram raises TypeError after figure allocation; label cardinality silently truncates line/histogram data; incomplete order raises raw KeyError after allocation; duplicate order and many non-finite inputs are accepted inconsistently.
findings.regression: No committed headless input-validation suite covers these cases.
findings.futureWork: Define input/cardinality/order/finite rules, validate before allocation, and add headless regressions for all five direct plot functions.

findings.title: Declared empty strip groups
findings.reproduction: Declare an ordered strip group with no observations and inspect summary marks and SVG output.
findings.observed: The browser emits an unused-group median of NaN, a non-finite terminal mark, and NaN SVG geometry; Python/browser policy is not defined.
findings.regression: No empty-category policy test exists.
findings.futureWork: Maintainer must decide whether empty declared categories are invalid, omitted, or rendered with an explicit empty-state semantic.

findings.title: Scene-contract identity
findings.reproduction: Compile equivalent portable contracts in Python and browser and compare objects labelled figurestead.scene/1.
findings.observed: Both use figurestead.scene/1 for materially different schemas; Python strip scene compilation still has zero marks.
findings.regression: No cross-runtime scene-schema conformance gate exists.
findings.futureWork: Product decision on whether scenes are runtime-internal or a versioned interchange contract; do not redesign under this audit.

findings.title: Large-array extent
findings.reproduction: Call extent() with a bounded array of 200,000 finite numbers.
findings.observed: Math.min(...values)/Math.max(...values) raises RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
findings.regression: No large-array extent test exists.
findings.futureWork: Replace spread extrema with an iterative finite scan and add bounded size/edge-case tests.

findings.title: First success and landing pages
findings.reproduction: Follow exact root README Python/browser links and execute both; inspect the npm-packed README source.
findings.observed: Both exact first-success examples run successfully. web/README.md remains a short boundary note without first success.
findings.regression: README audit covers root story and links, not npm landing first success.
findings.futureWork: A small npm landing-documentation package synchronized to the accepted root quickstart.

findings.title: Runtime and extension feature boundary
findings.reproduction: Inventory direct Python plots, portable builders, browser root registry, extension exports, and specimen wording.
findings.observed: README/specimen wording now truthfully discloses asymmetry, including Python-only matrix work. No complete feature matrix exists and categorical browser definitions remain absent.
findings.regression: Study audits protect current disclosure but do not enforce a repository-wide feature matrix.
findings.futureWork: Document a generated current feature matrix; do not add browser renderers in this package.

findings.title: Contributor, support, and security paths
findings.reproduction: Search tracked files for CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, SECURITY, SUPPORT, changelog, issue/PR templates, and inspect CLI discoverability.
findings.observed: None of the governance/support files or templates exists; four Python CLIs remain largely undiscovered.
findings.regression: No repository-policy documentation check exists.
findings.futureWork: A documentation-only maintainer path package covering support/security/reporting, contribution setup, and CLI index.

findings.title: Dependency policy
findings.reproduction: Inspect dependency floors and workflow coverage for advisory scans and minimum/latest matrices.
findings.observed: Broad minimums remain with no committed advisory/minimum-version policy, scan workflow, or minimum/latest matrix; no vulnerability is inferred from this fact alone.
findings.regression: No dependency-policy gate exists.
findings.futureWork: Define supported floors, add minimum/latest test environments and an advisory scan with explicit response policy.

findings.title: npm provenance and candidate identity
findings.reproduction: Inspect the workflow, retained candidate tree, public registry metadata, and packed package.json.
findings.observed: Workflow uses GitHub OIDC with supported Node/npm and does not disable provenance. Registry exposes a signature but no dist.attestations; no retained digest-bound candidate exists. Public tarball SHA-256 is 7b3e756c5193d53205925060a5005340a8e57a62550a720253a67391787ebe6a and has no local absolute paths.
findings.regression: No candidate-to-registry identity gate can run because the retained candidate is absent.
findings.futureWork: Restore candidate retention/preflight, then verify digest and provenance metadata without publishing.

findings.title: Version synchronization
findings.reproduction: Inventory version spellings across manifests, runtime constants, docs, site, workflows, and retained release paths.
findings.observed: Current Python and SemVer spellings are coherent, but no single mechanical check covers all public/release locations.
findings.regression: No repository-wide version synchronization check exists.
findings.futureWork: Add a read-only version consistency validator with explicit PEP 440/SemVer mapping.

findings.title: Frozen-site acceptance model
findings.reproduction: Inspect current R3 asset manifests, deploy validator, and site stewardship documentation.
findings.observed: R3 added strong canonical/derivative evidence and deploy validation. site/README.md still does not describe full generation, review, acceptance, rollback, and ownership.
findings.regression: Deploy validator checks artifacts, not stewardship process completeness.
findings.futureWork: Documentation-only frozen-site lifecycle and rollback ownership guide.

findings.title: Public-site asset cost
findings.reproduction: Read R3 manifest and verify derivative routes, srcset/lazy delivery, and canonical links.
findings.observed: R3 retains 69,380,331 canonical bytes and serves 2,127,517 lossless bytes, a 96.934% saving, with responsive derivatives and canonical inspection routes.
findings.regression: Pages deploy validator and R3 asset manifest cover this boundary.

findings.title: Compatibility and package metadata
findings.reproduction: Inspect engine/support declarations, Python metadata, and tested-version evidence.
findings.observed: npm declares Node >=24 <25; Python lacks authors, classifiers, and keywords; no declared-versus-tested support matrix exists.
findings.regression: No compatibility metadata validator exists.
findings.futureWork: Define tested support, align engine/runtime declarations, and complete package metadata without changing release versions.

findings.title: Static-site defense and failure resilience
findings.reproduction: Inspect document security metadata and the top-level public-alpha-set fetch failure path.
findings.observed: Overview/Atlas have no CSP or referrer policy; site/app.js throws at module top level when public-alpha-set.json fails.
findings.regression: Current R3 checks do not inject this asset failure or require security metadata.
findings.futureWork: A separate accepted-R3 resilience/security-header review; this turn deliberately leaves the baseline untouched.

findings.title: Accessibility annotation text
findings.reproduction: Render an evidence-bound/focus-bound anchorId annotation and inspect the generated hidden companion text.
findings.observed: The real DOM contains: Focus annotation: Evidence-bound peak at x undefined, y undefined.
findings.regression: V2 companion tests cover hidden focus and headings, not this annotation-description path.
findings.futureWork: Resolve anchor references before prose generation and add DOM assertions for evidence-bound and coordinate-bound annotations.

findings.title: Configuration transactionality
findings.reproduction: Render a valid line contract, call setConfig({panels: []}), catch the error, and compare renderer/controller/companion state.
findings.observed: The rejected update changes controller renderers from ['line'] to [] while the prior accessibility companion remains attached.
findings.regression: No failed-update rollback regression exists.
findings.futureWork: Validate/resolve replacement configuration before mutating controller, playback, renderer, or companion state; assert atomic rollback.

findings.title: Consumer types and formatting boundary
findings.reproduction: Search the shipped packages for .d.ts and py.typed; inspect formatter/lint configuration and count source/site lines over 240 characters.
findings.observed: No .d.ts or py.typed is shipped, no formatting boundary is configured, and the inspected source/site set contains 103 lines over 240 characters.
findings.regression: No type-presence or formatting gate exists.
findings.futureWork: Add consumer type artifacts and a narrowly scoped formatting policy in separate reviewable changes.
